entries.name: Chester date letter b, 1752-53
entries.means: Hallmarked at Chester in the assay year 1752-53; the letter changed in late spring or summer, not on 1 January.
entries.note: Mixed small and capital Roman letters in this cycle. Jackson 1921 and silvermakersmarks agree on the year; Chaffers 1924 starts the cycle a year later (A = 1752-53) with all capitals and a J, so its years differ. Case settled 2026-11-24: lower-case roman per Bradbury's Book of Hallmarks p. 52, Pickford's Jackson's Hallmarks (1991) p. 96 and Ridgway, Chester Silver (1985), Series 4 table; Ridgway pp. 32-34 calls Jackson 1921's capital alternatives a misreading of the copper plate.

visual.method: The letter b (lower-case roman, from this table) in the cycle's punch outline, a rectangle-rounded (Small upright rectangle with rounded corners around a roman letter, lower case to about O, capitals after), per Sir Charles J. Jackson, English Goldsmiths and Their Marks (1921), facsimiles; Bradbury's Book of Hallmarks. The letterform is a matching typeface, not the office's own punch.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: Chester date letter U, 1770-71
entries.means: Hallmarked at Chester in the assay year 1770-71; the letter changed in late spring or summer, not on 1 January.
entries.note: Disputed. 1770-71 per Ridgway, Chester Silver 1727-1837 (1985), pp. 32-34, and Pickford's Jackson's Hallmarks (1991), with silvermakersmarks. Jackson 1921: 1771-2, from Scasebrick's evidence to Parliament (1773), which Ridgway reads as a mishearing of W; no plate with a 1771 U is recorded. Chaffers 1924: 1772-73. entries.name: Chester date letter V, 1771-72
entries.means: Hallmarked at Chester in the assay year 1771-72; the letter changed in late spring or summer, not on 1 January.
entries.note: Disputed. 1771-72 per Ridgway (1985, pp. 32-34, V in a quatrefoil) and Pickford's Jackson's Hallmarks (1991), with silvermakersmarks. Jackson 1921: '1773'. Chaffers 1924 has no V in this cycle. (Restored 2026-11-24.)

visual.method: The letter V (upper-case roman, from this table) in the cycle's punch outline, a rectangle-rounded (Small upright rectangle with rounded corners around a roman letter, lower case to about O, capitals after), per Sir Charles J. Jackson, English Goldsmiths and Their Marks (1921), facsimiles; Bradbury's Book of Hallmarks. The letterform is a matching typeface, not the office's own punch.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: Britannia
entries.looks_like: A seated female figure with a shield and spear.
entries.means: From 27 Mar 1697 the Britannia standard (95.8% silver) was compulsory. Its marks are the figure of Britannia and a lion's head erased, in place of the lion passant and leopard's head. Sterling was allowed again from 1 Jun 1720, and Britannia stayed optional afterwards. From 1697 to 1701 only London could assay; Chester used Britannia marks 1701-1719/20.
